thread:
marta: Heads up — trying to cut release window now but deploy-bot failed artifact verify on canary. Holding cut. :no_entry_sign:

deploy-bot: FAILED verifying manifest for image redwood/service-api:2026-03-23-canary
  reason: layer 5 checksum mismatch (expected 3a7f..., got 0000...)
  action: holding promotion to prod

alex: hmm zero-bytes in a layer? that's usually multipart-upload or s3 eventual consistency. any s3 errors in the upload logs?

marta: attaching minimal logs below (from deploy-bot):
```
UPLOAD: s3://redwood-artifacts/service-api/2026-03-23/part-0005 size=0
Manifest verify: expected_sha=3a7f2c... actual_sha=000000...
Retrying 3/3 then fail
```

lee: @marta can you check CI restore logs too — last time TTL regen caused a thundering restore that produced partial uploads.

ci-bot: CI restore summary for build/3821:
- cache-restore: success for deps layer
- artifact-upload: multipart retry 2/3 then 503 from s3-put
- upload finalization: reported success but subsequent GET returned 0 bytes

sasha: ok that matches an eventual-consistency partial commit. Options: 1) reupload artifact + re-sign manifest, 2) pin to last-good image and hotfix upload asynchronously, 3) manual promote (dangerous).

alex: I'd prefer reupload then manual verify. Re-signing is fast if we have the artifact. Do we have the original builder node logs?

marta: builder logs exist on buildkite-agent/3821, but artifact reupload will take ~10m. Change window is 30m. If reupload succeeds we still need to re-run canary smoke (5m) and then promote.

lee: if reupload fails, fallback is pin to last-good image (2026-03-22-canary-good) and proceed. That avoids blocking customers but delays the new binary. Which do we prefer?

alex: safety-first: reupload now. i'll trigger an adhoc upload with the signed package from the build artifact store.

alex: running:
```
aws s3 cp /mnt/build/artifacts/service-api.tar s3://redwood-artifacts/service-api/2026-03-23/ --expected-size 124MB --acl bucket-owner-full-control
deployctl verify-manifest --image redwood/service-api:2026-03-23-canary
```

deploy-bot: Upload detected. Verifying manifest...

deploy-bot: ERROR: head-object returned 200 but content-length=0 for key part-0005 — transient S3 issue. Will retry 30s.

marta: noted. @lee can you watch the canary smoke once upload finishes?

lee: on it. also flagging infra to check s3 upload success metrics for the last hour. @infra-team :eyes: 

sasha: if we see repeated 0-byte parts we should enable single-part uploads for this artifact as emergency mitigation (slower but avoids multipart commit race).

alex: reupload succeeded, manifest verify passed. deploy-bot: canary rollout resumed.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for redwood/service-api:2026-03-23-canary -> 10% traffic. Smoke tests running.

lee: smoke green. 5/5 checks passed. holding 5m observation then promote.

marta: decision: reupload + verify worked. We'll proceed with promote after 5m observation. Recording action items:
- infra: investigate S3 0-byte multipart commits (ticket INFRA-827)
- build: add single-part fallback for >10MB artifacts when multipart fails (PR queued)
- release: update notes with short blurb about transient artifact issue and that canary was reuploaded

alex: 👍 I'll post final promote and release notes once prod promote completes.

deploy-bot: Promotion to prod scheduled at 1748010300 (after observation window).

marta: thanks all :thumbsup:
